summary: Frontend-only verification completed for all 7 required inner routes on the public URL. Route rendering, mapped section presence, shared header/footer/quote modal/WhatsApp/icon system, required navigation links, rice catalogue interactions, quote modal flow, contact form flow, and homepage isolation from inner assets passed. MOCKED flows confirmed: quote submission, contact submission, and newsletter submission are demo/toast-only frontend behavior.

integration_issues.issue: A single jump-to-bottom automation pattern left some .inner-reveal elements unrevealed on select pages, but stepped human-like scrolling revealed all content consistently.
Quote, contact, and newsletter submissions are MOCKED frontend flows showing demo toast only (no backend persistence).

action_items: Optional hardening: add a safety fallback in reveal logic so elements cannot remain hidden if observer misses a threshold under abrupt scroll jumps.
Retain /inner.css and /inner.js loading only on inner pages; keep homepage isolated as currently implemented.
critical_code_review_comments: All inner routes correctly use shared system injection via inner.js and include robust data-testid coverage for critical interactions.
Homepage correctly avoids loading inner.css and inner.js, preserving scope separation.
No framework runtime evidence was observed in tested inner page execution path (vanilla + jQuery flow active).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop run passed all requested flows. Mobile run passed navigation/forms/overflow and image checks. A jump-scroll-only reveal edge case appeared once but did not reproduce with stepped user-like scrolling. Keep focus on optional reveal fallback hardening if desired.
rca of the issue: Potential reveal fragility source: IntersectionObserver-triggered reveal classes depend on viewport intersection timing. Abrupt automated jump-to-bottom can bypass intended entry events for some sections; incremental scrolling reliably triggers reveal and resolves it.
